appraisal_events.evidence: Saint-Loup touches his hat and asks politely, "Monsieur, est-ce que vous voudriez bien jeter votre cigare, la fumée fait mal à mon ami"; the journalist answers "Il n'est pas défendu de fumer, que je sache ; quand on est malade, on n'a qu'à rester chez soi."
appraisal_events.explanation: A courteous request made with every mark of rank is refused flat by a man of none, and within the window Saint-Loup has no answer; the exchange is reported in bare dialogue.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Sa maîtresse, ne l'attendant pas, s'en allait vers sa loge", and calls across the theatre to the dancer, in a voice "facticement mélodieuse et innocente d'ingénue", "je crois qu'on pourrait très bien s'entendre avec toi et une de mes amies."
appraisal_events.explanation: She walks off without waiting for him and, in front of the house, proposes herself to another man; the narration marks the falseness of her voice but reports the disregard itself without comment.

status_effects.explanation: His politeness carries no force: the request is publicly rebuffed and turned back on the friend he was protecting, and he is left holding the courteous register alone.
His mistress does not wait for him and openly solicits the dancer in his hearing; the leverage in the relation is visibly hers.

ambiguities: "Sa maîtresse" is not named in the window; she is resolved to Rachel from the chapter's reference sheet rather than from the passage itself.
The journalist is unnamed and not on the reference sheet, so the source of E1 is recorded as unknown even though the passage attributes the retort plainly to him.
